_about: Authority normalization table (SITE-PLAN Phase 4 pilot, 2026-11-06). Author sigla -> canonical author; per author, work abbreviations -> canonical work. Built from the pilot slice (Vol I d.1-10, Breviloquium, Ecclesiastes) and extended only from measured residue. Matching (tools/build-authorities.py): asterisks stripped, points optional, spacing free, CASE-SENSITIVE (Quaracchi capitalizes a work abbreviation, not a locus: 'Serm. 362' is a work, 'Enarrat. in Ps. 118, serm. 13' is a locus), longest match first, work matched only inside its own author's scope. Attribution follows Quaracchi: 'pseudo': true only where the attribution is modern consensus AND Quaracchi's own notes treat it so; the English name may use the modern scholarly form. 'here' marks the work a same-passage citation (hic / in hunc locum) of a scholastic means: his commentary on the Sentences.
same_passage: in suo Comment. in hunc locum

authors._note: Lombard's Sentences are NOT an authority record: they are in this corpus (the littera chunks) and are the cross-reference ledger's business. Only his other works are indexed here.
The siglum itself names the work (Decret. Gregor. = the Decretals), so a bare locus takes default_work.

witness_context: A work matched where the editors REPORT A WITNESS'S READING (cod./codd./ed./edd./Vat./mss. ... allegat/citat/legit, or 'falso alleget') is not an authority record: it is the apparatus criticus.
_body_join: A note giving ONLY a locus (Libr. X. c. 33.) takes its author from the body text before its anchor: the nearest name in 'body' within 220 characters. A title with no siglum whose abbreviation belongs to exactly ONE author takes that author. Both are marked in 'via' (body-join / unique-title) so they can be audited apart.
_prose: 'prose' lists the forms a work takes in running Latin (in libro Confessionum), for the body join; they are tried before the stemmed Latin title.
